claims.text: The example alloy is equiatomic bcc HfNbTaTiZr.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy has a disordered or random atomic distribution.
The initial alloy has adequate high-temperature strength for use as an intermediate layer.
A controlled intermediate-temperature annealing treatment can promote chemical short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr.
Annealing can induce ordered clustering without causing grain coarsening.
Temperatures up to about 700 °C, with mechanical loading and irradiation, are representative service conditions for intermediate plasma-facing reactor components.
Chemical short-range order produces ordered clusters in equiatomic bcc HfNbTaTiZr.
Short-range order reduces atomic displacements and local lattice distortion.
The reduction in local distortion caused by short-range order reduces phonon scattering.
The SRO-containing microstructure acts like a composite with a matrix containing fewer atomic-level defects.
Reduced phonon scattering increases lattice thermal conductivity.
Phase stability and retention of the grain structure preserve mechanical integrity after SRO-promoting annealing.
SRO-promoting annealing will increase lattice thermal conductivity by approximately 10–12% relative to the disordered baseline.
Mechanical strength and ductility will remain at or above current intermediate-layer performance levels after annealing.
The SRO-induced thermal and mechanical effects will persist up to approximately 700 °C under typical reactor loading.
Avoiding deleterious grain growth and unwanted phase transformations is necessary for the claimed benefit.
Simulation results show approximately a 12% increase in lattice thermal conductivity at maximum SRO relative to random HfNbTaTiZr.
The magnitude of the benefit under practical irradiated plasma-facing conditions and its long-term effect on irradiation resistance are uncertain.
